name: Megasoma vogti
intro: I received and photographed second-instar larvae. Their hatch dates were unknown.

facts.title: Published brood origin
facts.text: Female collected in Live Oak County, Texas

facts.title: Adult habitat
facts.text: Mesquite scrub in southern Texas and northeastern Mexico

sections.title: Larvae
sections.text: Ratcliffe and Morón described and illustrated a third instar reared from an egg laid by a female collected in Live Oak County, Texas, in October 1989.

sections.title: Adults
sections.text: Field records extend from July through October in habitats with mesquite, thorn shrubs and cacti. Both sexes have been found at lights, on the ground and on mesquite branches. The larval food in these sites is undetermined.

sources.title: Ratcliffe and Morón (2005), third instar reared from an egg of a Texas female
University of Nebraska State Museum, Megasoma vogti

account_credit: Breeding notes by Junkai Wang and Alan Jeon

gallery.caption: Second-instar larvae in my care in July 2022.
gallery.alt: Several pale, curled Megasoma vogti larvae on the surface of a rearing box.

distribution.caption: The museum account places this scarab in Texas and Tamaulipas, Mexico. In Texas it occupies southern thornscrub.
distribution.alt: Documented regions for Megasoma vogti: Tamaulipas, Texas.
